I have farmed this land in Quzhou County for 50 years, and I know every corner of my 10.1 mu. My children work off-farm in the city, so it is mainly me and my wife managing the fields, with help from relatives during busy harvest and planting times. At 70 years old, I do not chase every new technique, but I have learned what works here on the North China Plain. The wheat-maize rotation has fed my family for decades, and I will stick with it.

For the winter wheat, I will plant an improved variety that my neighbors and I have relied on — it resists the dry spring winds and gives steady yields. I will prepare the land with rotary tillage before October sowing, spread about 16 kg of nitrogen, 6 kg of phosphorus, and 4 kg of potassium per mu as base and topdressing, and irrigate four times: once before winter to ensure good emergence, once at green-up, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. I will spray pesticide twice if the aphids or rust appear. I expect around 500 kg per mu if the spring drought is not too severe.

For the summer maize, I will sow hybrid seed immediately after the wheat harvest in early June — there is no time to waste. I will use no-tillage sowing into the wheat stubble to save time and moisture, which is how most of us do it now. I will apply about 15 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu, irrigate three times (jointing, big trumpet, and filling stages), and spray pesticide twice for corn borers and armyworms. With good weather and well water, I expect about 550 kg per mu from the maize.

decision.reasoning_summary: After 50 years farming this same wheat-maize rotation in Quzhou County, I know that timing and water matter more than fancy inputs. I will plant improved wheat in winter with rotary tillage, four irrigations, and modest fertilizer, then follow immediately with hybrid maize using no-tillage to catch the short summer growing window. These are the practices that have kept my household fed and provided a little extra grain to sell, and at my age I trust what has worked on this soil.
